title: All eyes on November in Virginia with congressional primaries in rearview mirror - NewsBreak
text:
By Tyler Englander ,
1 hours ago
RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) – With nominees selected, all eyes are on the November midterm elections in Virginia.
Randolph-Macon Political Science professor Rich Meagher said this year’s congressional primaries in Virginia went as expected, with all the frontrunners winning.
“Setting up the big battles that we were expecting for this fall,” Meagher told 8News.
Meagher said as Virginians turn their attention to November, the national political landscape will play a key factor in all of Virginia’s congressional races, including the most competitive.
“I think the overall environment here is favorable towards Democrats, in part, just because of how the economy’s doing,” Meagher said. “And the economy’s mixed right now, right, there’s good news in the stock market, but I think people are really feeling the pinch of inflation, prices at the gas pump, and they do blame the Trump administration and Donald Trump himself for that, and they blame the Republicans.”
IN ROANOKE: City Council candidates, Mayor Cobb react to Democratic Primary The race for Virginia’s First Congressional District features incumbent Republican Congressman Rob Wittman running against Democratic Henrico County Commonwealth’s Attorney Shannon Taylor.
“The Wittman-Taylor battle is maybe gonna be determined much less by those two and more about the national mood and what’s happening in Washington,” Meagher said.
Meanwhile, the race for Virginia’s Second Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Congresswoman Jen Kiggans against former Democratic Congresswoman Elaine Luria.
REGIONAL FOCUS: Midterm races set for Virginia’s 5th, 6th and 9th congressional districts “The fact that Kiggans defeated Luria last time in an environment that was really anti-Democrat, right, because of what was going on in Washington, I think the reverse could happen this year where Luria defeats Kiggans because of an environment that’s anti-Republican,” Meagher said.
Meanwhile, in Virginia’s U.S. Senate race, Meagher thinks despite his win in Tuesday’s Republican Primary, retired Army Major General Bert Mizusawa remains a heavy underdog against Democratic Senator Mark Warner.
“Mark Warner, as a longtime incumbent with a huge war chest, it’s just really stacked up against Mizusawa.”
Early voting for the midterm elections begins on Sept. 18.
